1 niece of the informant was beaten very badly and an attempt to throttle was also made, as a result whereof, she became unconscious.
It was also stated that the informant had seen that the matrimonial family beaten the victim.
It was stated that subsequently, she was taken to the hospital and ultimately she died before the treatment could be given.
4. In the light of the aforesaid, the submission of the counsel for the applicant is that in the inquest report, it was recorded that no injuries were noticed except on the neck, a mark was noted.
He further argues that however, in the postmortem, as many as, 10 injuries were noticed on various parts of the body.
He further argues that at the time of inquest, the husband was present.
The applicant had took the victim to the hospital also.
As per the postmortem report, the cause of death is due to ante mortem strangulation.
He further argues that two of the fact witnesses have been examined out of the total 19 witnesses proposed to be examined.
He lastly argues that all the co-accused have been enlarged on bail.
The applicant is in custody since 22.08.2023 and has no criminal history, as such, the applicant may be enlarged on bail.

5. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer by arguing that apart from the cause of death as determined in the postmortem report, prima facie, as many as 10 injuries were noticed on the body of the deceased and in terms of the two statements recorded, the implication of the applicant is wholly justified, as such, the bail application may be rejected.
It is however not disputed that the applicant has no criminal antecedents.

6. Considering the fact that only two fact witnesses have been examined and cross-examined and there is no likelihood of the trial being concluded in near future and thus without going into the analysis of the evidence recorded so far, prima facie, no material exists to come to the conclusion that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicantAshraf be released on bail in the abovesaid first information report number on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
